content.name: Iván Manfredi

current.headline: Agency owners: add $15k-$50k/mo from LinkedIn in 90 days with content + outreach, run for you.
current.about_excerpt: Agency owner doing 6 or 7 figures a year? Want to add $15k-$60k/mo of revenue from LinkedIn, all run for you? Read this 👇 Because you're on my profile, a few things I'd bet are true: 1. You know LinkedIn can get you clients, you just never get around to the content or the outreach 2. You tried a ghostwriter, and the posts didn't sound like you 3. You tried a lead-gen agency, and months of...

diagnosis.point: Your headline promises a revenue range with nothing attached to it. A stranger reading it has no way to check whether anyone has ever hit $15k-$50k/mo with you, because the one client number you own, Kyle Hunt going from $30k to $80k a month, sits on your website and never appears on the profile. The claim reads as a template until the name and the number carry it.
diagnosis.quote: Agency owners: add $15k-$50k/mo from LinkedIn in 90 days with content + outreach, run for you.

diagnosis.point: Your headline says $15k-$50k and your About says $15k-$60k. Same profile, two numbers, ten seconds apart for anyone who scrolls. A buyer weighing whether you handle detail on their account reads that gap before they read your offer.
diagnosis.quote: Want to add $15k-$60k/mo of revenue from LinkedIn, all run for you? Read this

diagnosis.point: Your About opens by guessing what the reader has already tried, five items of it, before it says what you do. The reader arrived because they already know their own problem. The first screen spends itself on a list they could have written, and your only named proof, 1,008 invites and 11 booked calls for Mattan Danino, never gets a line.
diagnosis.quote: Because you're on my profile, a few things I'd bet are true:

diagnosis.point: Your second experience entry carries the hardest numbers on the profile: 100+ systems shipped, $5M+ in documented client savings, $100k+ in solo contract revenue. None of it reaches the headline or the About, so the buyer has to scroll past the offer to find the evidence for it. That ordering asks a stranger to do work they will not do.
diagnosis.source_label: your AI Systems Architect & Workflow Automation entry at Manfredi
diagnosis.quote: • 100+ systems shipped — intake forms, qualification rubrics, support agents, internal workflows

headlines.text: Named leads in your inbox and calls on your calendar while you stay heads-down on client work.
headlines.why: You describe the end state the founder pictures at 7pm when the delivery work is done and the pipeline is empty, in the words they would use themselves. It sounds like every other promise they have been sold, so the profile below it has to land hard.

headlines.text: I run LinkedIn for agency founders: content and outreach done for you, about 15 minutes a week on your side.
headlines.why: It names exactly who you serve and hands the burned-out founder the one number that matters to them, the time they have to give up. You give up any proof, so it reads as a promise until they click through to the case studies.

headlines.text: Kyle Hunt went from $30k to $80k a month in the 90 days I ran his LinkedIn.
headlines.why: A named coach with a before and after does the convincing that adjectives cannot, and this buyer already coaches or consults so Kyle is a mirror. It gives up any mention of what you actually do, so the click has to carry the explanation.

about.text:
You already know LinkedIn could fill your calendar. You just have client work to deliver, and nobody to run the content and the outreach while you do it.

I run LinkedIn as a revenue line for agency founders: content plus outreach, done for you, 24/7. Today I run [add your current client count] accounts.

Kyle Hunt coaches ecomm and digital-marketing agency owners and is an 8-figure agency COO. His business went from $30k to $80k a month across the 90 days I ran his LinkedIn.

[add a client quote naming the result]

He is at 28,845 followers with 59 lead magnets in his pipeline as of July 2026, and his comment-gated lead-magnet posts have pulled over 1,600 comments. That plan is $2k a month, fixed.

For Mattan Danino, who runs the performance-only growth agency RISE DTC in Los Angeles, I sent 1,008 connection invites, got 294 accepts, 119 replies and 11 booked calls.

His lead magnets live on his own domain at resources.risedtc.com, so the emails land on his list and stay there.

The posts come out of your own recorded sales and client calls, so they argue what you already argue to buyers all day. No blank page, no writer guessing at your voice.

Your part is about 15 minutes a week: approve or veto. Then take the calls.

My site counts $2M in client revenue generated, $50M in pipeline built and 50+ brands served. Before this I built AI and automation systems for $1-10M service businesses, 100+ shipped, $5M+ in documented client savings.

I ran my whole pipeline off one Upwork profile for two years before I moved to LinkedIn. Now leads land in my inbox already knowing what I do, and I charge triple what I ever cleared there.

Typical time to first booked call is [add your typical time to first booked call].

Send me a message and I will tell you whether your calls have enough in them to build on.
about.first_lines_note: Your first two lines name the reader's exact situation, a founder who already believes in LinkedIn and has no hours, so the person you want feels described before they decide to click. The second line hands them the missing piece, someone to run content and outreach, which makes see more the obvious next move.

swap_notes: Swap [add your current client count] for the real number, because two named clients read as two lucky accounts and a client count tells a buyer you run a system.

Put a real founder quote in place of [add a client quote naming the result], because the $30k to $80k line is where a burned buyer starts doubting, and another founder saying it carries weight your own claim cannot.

Replace [add your typical time to first booked call] with your real timeline, because that is the question they will ask on the fit call anyway, and answering it first removes the last reason to stall.
